hypothesis: Unmapped blind faults concentrate at tip-to-tip relay bridges and distal intrabasin stepovers of USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue; targeting tip extrapolations (0.6-1.2 km) plus distal corridors (>2 km) recovers blind faults hidden by Quaternary alluvium better than catalogue-proximal density methods.
mechanism: Catalogue geometry only: PCA strike on 7-px trace window per tip, 6-12 px forward extrapolation (100 m grid), 0.5-2.0 km tip-pair straight bridges with <30° collinearity, plus distal >2 km pool thinned to 3-px spacing (18827+18827 dots), binary 1 px dots, collar >2 px off mapped faults, outside-footprint zero, EPSG:32611 3730x3292 float32 [0,1].
named_non_fault_process: Unfaulted paleovalley margins, caldera moat walls, and Miocene lava-flow lobe terminations mimic tip-rectilinear geometry without tectonic slip; pluvial shorelines mimic distal lineaments.
